name: Ethotoin

similar.name: Oxyphenbutazone Anhydrous
problems: Pulled from the market in United States and 7 other countries, first in 1984 — for blood problems and serious skin reactions

summary: Ethotoin has no recorded safety issues of its own listed here [1][2]. According to a small computer model rather than tests on people, it received a medium risk score of 54 for the liver and a low risk score of 39 for the heart [M]. A similar drug called Oxyphenbutazone Anhydrous was pulled from the market in the United States and seven other countries starting in 1984 due to blood-related harm and skin-related harm [3].
